incidents.name: Apollo 1
incidents.text: During a test on the launch pad, with the hatches closed and the cabin filled with pure oxygen, a flash fire swept through the spacecraft. All three astronauts died.
incidents.quote: Because of the pure oxygen atmosphere, the fire spread quickly, causing a rapid rise in temperature and pressure that led to the rupture of the Command Module pressure vessel.
incidents.sourceTitle: NASA Safety and Mission Assurance: Apollo 1
support: On Jan. 27, Grissom, White and Chaffee were scheduled to conduct a key test on the launch pad
The astronauts would be wearing spacesuits with the spacecraft’s hatches closed and the cabin pressurized with 100% oxygen.
During the test, a flash fire swept through the spacecraft so quickly, there was no time to open the hatches.
By the time the pad crew was able to open the hatches, the crew had already perished.

incidents.name: Mir
incidents.text: An oxygen generator caught fire, blocked the way to an escape craft and filled the station with smoke. The crew fought it until it went out, with no lasting harm to the crew.
incidents.quote: On Feb. 24, 1997, the six crew members aboard the Russian space station Mir faced significant danger when a fire ignited in an oxygen generating system.
incidents.sourceTitle: NASA History: 25 Years Ago: Fire Aboard Space Station Mir
support: The searing flame, lasting several minutes, not only cut off access to one of the two Soyuz escape vehicles but also filled the station’s modules with smoke.
the crew prevailed and extinguished the flames
with no lasting harm to the crew members

video.title: The Power of Studying Combustion on the ISS
video.quote: Scientists are learning more about combustion through a series of experiments on the International Space Station.
video.sourceTitle: NASA Image and Video Library: The Power of Studying Combustion on the ISS
